# Turf

> The infrastructure engine built for AI agents. Turf plans, applies, and converges
> Terraform-compatible infrastructure at any scale — driven by agents in natural language
> or HCL. Every change is planned, visible, and approved before it happens.

Turf is Terraform-compatible infrastructure as code exposed to AI agents as an MCP server,
built on OpenTofu providers. It runs your existing configurations — HCL, modules, providers —
unchanged. The engine (`turf-mcp-server`) is the product; the Turf CLI (`turf`) is one way to
consume it, and any MCP client is another. Installing with `brew install turfbuild/tap/turf`
puts both on your PATH.

The governing idea: Turf produces the plan, and the Terraform plan becomes the agent's TODO
list — worked one effect at a time, with an approval gate between rounds. Nothing runs
off-plan. Turf is alpha software; some capabilities are marked coming soon on the site.

## Start here

- [Get started](https://turf.build/get-started/): install the CLI and MCP server, wire it into Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code, or any MCP client, and run a first plan.
- [Compatibility](https://turf.build/compatibility/): a three-way comparison of Terraform 1.14, OpenTofu 1.12, and Turf — what is supported today, where Turf is ahead (actions, deferred changes), and what is coming soon.
- [Kubernetes stack demo](https://turf.build/demo/): a kind cluster, a CRD, and a custom resource converged in one governed run, then torn down.
- [Scalr integration demo](https://turf.build/demo/scalr/): folding an existing Terraform automation platform's state backend, variables, and OPA policy checks into the plan.

## Use cases

The five positioning pillars, all covered at [turf.build/#use-cases](https://turf.build/#use-cases):

- **Terraform at 10x scale** — thousands of resources per stack; a durable, scale-out engine parallelizes provider operations until the cloud API, not the tool, is the ceiling. Run a Kubernetes cluster as a control plane for infrastructure ops, or run it all on a laptop.
- **Datacenter automation** — orchestrate the build-out of servers, networks, Kubernetes, and workloads. Terraform, Ansible, and Helm converge in one governed run via Terraform actions. Day-2 operations are plannable too.
- **Autonomous products** — Turf as a smart installation tool for an AI-native application or data product: it automates the infrastructure layer, in your cloud or a customer's account, from any mix of HCL and natural language, and auto-detects and heals drift.
- **Governed AI operations** — every change planned, visible, and approved, with a gate between every round.
- **Agentic infrastructure as code** — an MCP server at its core, driven from any MCP client to plan and carry out any sort of infrastructure change.

## Source and examples

- [turfbuild/turf](https://github.com/turfbuild/turf): the Turf CLI and `turf-mcp-server`, alpha binary releases.
- [turfbuild/turf-examples](https://github.com/turfbuild/turf-examples): runnable HCL examples, agent definitions, and integrations.
- [turfbuild/opentofu](https://github.com/turfbuild/opentofu): the OpenTofu fork Turf builds on (MPL-2.0), alongside forks of the provider client and the tfcoremock test provider.
